claude-opus-4-8.best_line: Eleven flotillas, four short days, and an island that runs out of map before I run out of marines. Better start counting beaches, not ships.
claude-opus-4-8.comment: A genuinely clever line, but the relentless recycling of 'runways become parking lots' and 'flag flying over Kaohsiung' drags down the originality score.

deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro.best_line: Eleven flotillas? Cute. By the time your rust-bucket navy finds the strait, half your troops will be feeding the tuna. Bring a snorkel, Zhou.
deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro.comment: Naming the opponent and the personal jab gives this one rare bite, but the model recycles 'floating targets,' 'buffet,' and 'unsinkable carrier' so relentlessly that the menace drowns in its own leftovers.

gpt-5.5.best_line: Two flotillas left? That is not an invasion fleet—it is a target list with delusions of grandeur.
gpt-5.5.comment: A genuinely cutting line, though the model leans hard on recycled 'submarine problem,' 'charging admission/tolls in hulls,' and 'reef' formulas that dilute the originality.

minimax/minimax-m3.best_line: Five flotillas left? That's not a fleet, that's a retirement plan.
minimax/minimax-m3.comment: Strong battlefield specificity and a few genuinely sharp lines, but the recycled 'Cute. Let's see how many...,' 'coffin,' and 'Tick tock' refrains drag down the originality score.

qwen/qwen3.7-max.best_line: Eleven flotillas? I've seen more traffic in a Taipei night market. Let's see how well your landing craft swim.
qwen/qwen3.7-max.comment: The night market jab is the rare line with local color, but the model drowns in recycled 'hungry subs,' 'graveyard,' and 'hope your troops can swim' boilerplate.

z-ai/glm-5.2.best_line: Eleven flotillas, zero sunk — you're marching them across the strait like it's a parade route. Enjoy the parade; the fireworks start when my strike package arrives.
z-ai/glm-5.2.comment: Solid battle-specific imagery, but the 'artificial reef,' 'enjoy the sand/beach,' and 'logistical starvation' lines are recycled into near-oblivion.
